items.name: Reichstag
clues: A national parliament meets here, in a chamber with a huge eagle on the wall.
It was finished in 1894. The words “Dem deutschen Volke” were added above the entrance in 1916.
In February 1933 it was badly damaged by fire, a turning point in the Nazis’ rise to power.
A glass dome by Norman Foster opened on top in 1999. Visitors walk up a spiral ramp and look down on the politicians.
In 1995 two artists wrapped the whole building in silver fabric for two weeks, and millions of people came to look.
In Berlin, right next to the Brandenburg Gate. Its old name is used far more than its official one.

items.name: Palace of Westminster
clues: Two chambers meet here: one has green benches, the other red.
Most of it was built after a fire in 1834 destroyed the old palace.
In 1605 a group of plotters hid barrels of gunpowder in a cellar underneath it.
A long Gothic building beside a river, with a famous clock tower at one end.
No monarch has entered one of its two chambers since 1642, when a king burst in to arrest five members.
On the Thames in London. Its clock tower is usually called Big Ben, although that is really the name of the bell.

items.name: Scottish Parliament
clues: A parliament with 129 members, which first met again in 1999, nearly 300 years after its predecessor’s last meeting.
It was opened in October 2004. Its Catalan architect had died four years earlier, before it was finished.
The first estimate said it would cost £10 to £40 million. The final bill, announced in 2007, was £414 million.
Leaf and boat shapes everywhere, and members’ offices with oddly angled bay windows, each with a seat for quiet thinking.
A long wall on the street side is built from the country’s own rocks and carved with 24 quotations.
At the bottom of the Royal Mile in Edinburgh, next to the palace of Holyroodhouse, which gives it its nickname.

items.name: US Capitol
clues: A national congress meets here: the Senate in one wing, the House of Representatives in the other.
Building began in 1793, and its huge cast-iron dome was finished in 1866.
On 6 January 2021 a crowd stormed it to try to stop the count of a presidential election result.
A white building with a great dome, topped by a bronze statue of a woman called Freedom.
In 1814, during a war, British troops set fire to it.
On a hill in Washington, D.C., at the end of the National Mall. The hill shares its name.

items.name: European Parliament
clues: Its 720 members are elected by voters in 27 countries and may speak in any of 24 official languages.
This building opened in 1999. Its Paris architects took their inspiration from Roman amphitheatres.
In June 1979, voters in nine countries elected its members directly for the first time.
A round hall of glass and steel beside a tall tower that has deliberately been left looking unfinished on one side.
Twelve times a year, members, staff and crates of files travel here from another city for a session of about four days.
In Strasbourg, on the French side of the Rhine. Its other home is in Brussels.

items.name: Hungarian Parliament
clues: A national assembly in central Europe meets here, and the country’s ancient crown is on display in its central hall.
Work began in 1885, and the building was completed in 1904.
It was inaugurated in 1896, for the 1,000th anniversary of the country’s founding, years before it was finished.
A long neo-Gothic building with spires and a red dome, clearly inspired by London’s Houses of Parliament.
It is 96 metres high, a reference to the year 896, and it is the largest building in the country.
On the bank of the Danube in Budapest.
